Vanessa — saw the screenshot. Two quick troubleshooting points for calendar drift: 

1) Floating time vs anchored time: If the .ics event is created without an explicit TZ identifier (e.g., only a local timestamp), Google sometimes treats it as floating and converts relative to the recipient's default calendar zone. That explains a +1 hour shift when DST or CET labels are involved.

2) Best fix for cross-region customers: ask them to either (a) send a GCal invite from their calendar account (explicit TZ), or (b) include UTC times in the event title and body, plus an .ics anchored with a VTIMEZONE block.

If you want, I can create a fresh invite from redwood.ai with explicit UTC and CET instances and include a fallback Zoom link. I'll also pre-provision a 30-minute demo in the EU region so performance matches what they'll see in production.

Markus — looping you in in case we want to offer a morning APAC slot (they mentioned some Madrid folks might join remotely).

— Priyom
